inputs_used: content-system/seo/link-map.csv (grep greece, santorini, mykonos, crete, corfu, rhodes, orthodox, season, best-time, concierge, magazine)

payload.title: Best Time to Get Married in Greece by Month
payload.primary_keyword: best time to get married in greece
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more who have chosen Greece, or are close to it, and now need to pick a month before they can hold a venue or send save-the-dates: they want to know what the weather actually does from April to October on the islands they are considering, what the heat and wildfire advice says for guests, when venues open and close, and which religious and public dates to plan around, so they can choose a window that suits their guests and their ceremony and then hand the planning to someone who will look after it.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can match their preferred months to venue availability, travel and guest stays.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'best time to get married in greece' mostly name a single best month from general travel opinion, with unattributed temperatures and crowd claims. This guide refuses to name a winner. It gives a month-by-month picture from April to October built only on official Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS) station climate data, each figure labelled with its station (Naxos for the Cyclades, Rodos, Heraklion and Chania for Crete, Kerkyra for Corfu, Athens if sourced), adds Smartraveller's heat and wildfire advice as worded, the season windows venues state on their own sites, and the dates to plan around (Orthodox closed periods credited to the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia with 'ask your priest for Greece'; public holidays only from an official source). It ends with 'which months suit you' scenarios so the couple chooses for their own guests, ceremony and island.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: there is no single right month; the wedding season most venues state runs within roughly April to October [[VERIFY: venue-stated windows]]; the right month depends on island, heat tolerance, ceremony type and guests. Then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways, none naming a best month (weather differs by island and station; heat and wildfire advice for high summer as Smartraveller words it; venues state their own season windows; Orthodox closed periods and public holidays shape the calendar).

How to read the figures: one short section explaining the figures are HNMS long-term station averages (name the period if the source states it), each labelled with its station, averages not forecasts; no research talk.

Month-by-month table, April to October: columns for month, station, average maximum temperature, rainfall or rain days and sea temperature only where HNMS or another official source publishes it, and a short planning note. Every figure labelled with its station; any unsourced cell left blank or marked [[VERIFY]].

Month by month: a short subsection for each month April to October, using the table figures, Smartraveller heat and wildfire advice where relevant (as worded), and venue season windows as venues state them. No crowd claims unless officially sourced. No prices.

By island: Cyclades (Naxos station; link /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding, /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/paros-wedding-venues), Crete (Heraklion and Chania; link /destination-weddings/wedding-in-crete and /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues), Rhodes (Rodos; link /destination-weddings/rhodes-wedding-venues), Corfu (Kerkyra; link /destination-weddings/corfu-wedding-venues), Athens if sourced. Link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues once. Island guides keep their own season detail; this section summarises and links.

Dates to plan around: Orthodox closed periods (for example Lent and the Dormition fast) credited to the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia, with 'ask your priest for Greece', and Orthodox Easter dates from an official source; link /destination-weddings/greek-orthodox-wedding. Greek public holidays only if from an official Greek government source.

Which months suit you: 4 to 6 scenarios (for example a church ceremony, older or young guests sensitive to heat, a sunset ceremony on the Cyclades, a longer guest stay, swimming as part of the weekend), each pointing to months and islands from the figures, no single answer. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (brand-facts claims only, framed around matching months to venue availability, travel and guest stays), with a link to /wonderland-concierge.

FAQ (4 to 6): What month do most Greek venues open for weddings? How hot is Greece in July and August? Can we marry in a Greek Orthodox church at any time of year? Is October too late for a Greek island wedding? When does the sea warm up for guests? Answers from the same sources as the body, never naming a best month.

Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the definition line or its closing phrase). Links: /wonderland-concierge (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-greece&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Naming a single best month, or 'best', 'ideal', 'perfect' or ranking language anywhere in the body (title and keyword only).
Any temperature, rainfall or sea figure without its HNMS station (or other official source) label; figures from travel blogs, weather aggregators or Wikipedia.
Crowd, busy-season or tourist-number claims unless from an official source.
Any price, fee, discount or amount; 'off-season savings' or 'cheaper' claims; 'free'.
Transfers, drive, ferry or flight times.
Orthodox rules not credited to the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia; religious commentary; public holidays not from an official source.
Research talk in copy ('we could not confirm', 'on its own site'); per-line source credits beyond the station labels; hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs or their wording and images.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Advisor definition line and the phrase 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.
payload.cannibalisation_check: None found for 'best time to get married in greece': no URL in content-system/seo/link-map.csv targets it or a Greece-wide season variant. Overlap: /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding and /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding own their island season variants and /destination-weddings/wedding-in-crete has its own seasons section; they keep those, and this guide owns Greece-wide timing and month-by-month intent, summarising islands briefly and linking down. Island guides should link up to this page from their season sections. /destination-weddings/greek-orthodox-wedding owns Orthodox terms; this post gives the closed-period dates only and links. SEO to check variants (best month to get married in greece, greece wedding season, when to get married in santorini).

fact_check_batches.B: Smartraveller Greece heat and wildfire advice as worded, as at November 2026 (fact_100+)
